findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a coordination constraint so children creating/amending ADRs (1de3, 8537, 373f) land relative to 0743's renumbering, and 0743's resolution table accounts for concurrently-created ADR numbers and references.
evidence: 0743: 'The 17 duplicate numbers are resolved... 22 files move to numbers above 0061' and 'docs/adr/RENUMBERING.md records the old-to-new mapping and the per-reference resolution table'
1de3 AC: 'ADR 0035:192 is amended via the established `> **AMENDED by [rebar:<id>]**` convention'
373f: '~13 new ADRs are proposed across the shards'
8537 AC: 'ADR 0004 describes the enforcement that actually exists'
Neither 0743 nor 1de3/8537/373f names coordination of concurrently-changing ADR numbers/references
findings.finding: Cross-child residual-reference hazard: child 0743 renumbers 22 ADRs and rewrites ADR references repo-wide, while children 1de3 (amends 'ADR 0035:192'), 8537 (amends ADR 0004), and 373f (writes ~13 NEW ADRs) concurrently create or cite ADRs by number — but no child names the coordination, so an ADR number amended/created by one child may be renumbered by 0743, leaving a stale citation.
scenarios: 0743 renumbers ADR 0035 (or an ADR that 373f's new ADRs cite) after 1de3/373f have already written amendments/citations against the old number, producing a dangling reference that 0743's resolution table did not capture because the citation landed concurrently.
373f files new ADRs that claim numbers 0743 is simultaneously assigning to renumbered files, re-creating the exact collision class 0743 exists to eliminate.
findings.suggested_fix: Sequence 0743 after the ADR-creating/amending children, or have 0743's RENUMBERING resolution pass explicitly include the ADRs and citations produced by 1de3, 8537, and 373f.

evidence: 3 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Define the per-shard 'complete' condition for comment triage (e.g. every comment classified as move-candidate or do_not_move) so completion is observable.
evidence: 'Comment triage complete across all six subsystem shards'
No stated definition of 'complete' (e.g. every comment classified move/do_not_move) — signal (2) implicit acceptance criteria
findings.finding: The AC 'Comment triage complete across all six subsystem shards' does not define what makes a shard's triage 'complete'; 'complete' is an effort/completion term without a stated observable acceptance condition per shard beyond preserving a do_not_move list.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — 'Comment triage complete across all six subsystem shards, with each shard's do_not_move list preserved as the protection record'
scenarios: An executor triages some comments in a shard and marks it complete; a reviewer disputes whether the shard was fully covered.
findings.suggested_fix: State that a shard is complete when every comment in it is classified into either a moved/actioned set or the shard's do_not_move list, with the do_not_move list checked in as the record.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Inline the concrete mechanism for each non-mechanical AC (snapshot-entry CI check, exit-codes CI check, ADR-uniqueness guard, LLM-Review tree-binding) — for the ADR guard state whether it is a merge-time/pre-receive gate vs. a CI scan (and how it avoids a concurrent-merge TOCTOU); for the vote state which channel binds it to the reviewed tree (e.g. `verified_at_sha`).
evidence: AC: 'The snapshot-entry contract is enforced by CI rather than asserted by an ADR' — names the enforcement class, not the check
AC: 'ADR numbers uniquely identify a document, and a new collision cannot merge' — 'cannot merge' does not say whether it is a merge-time/pre-receive gate or a CI-side scan
AC: 'An LLM-Review vote provably attaches to the tree that was reviewed' — the binding channel is unnamed (the codebase already has `verified_at_sha` as the tree pin in src/rebar/signing.py)
ABSENCE: the plan body carries no per-AC mechanism; header defers detail to `.joe-janitor/report-2026-08-06.md`, absent from the snapshot
findings.finding: The plan states end-state goals but no chosen MECHANISM for the four non-mechanical ACs (snapshot-entry contract 'enforced by CI', exit-codes.md 'CI keeps it that way', ADR 'a new collision cannot merge', LLM-Review vote 'provably attaches to the tree that was reviewed'); the implementing approach is deferred to `.joe-janitor/report-2026-08-06.md`, which is not carried in the plan. Without the mechanism inlined, approach soundness (data-flow completeness, ordering/atomicity) cannot be judged.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria (snapshot-entry contract; docs/exit-codes.md; ADR numbers; LLM-Review vote)
scenarios: The ADR-collision guard is implemented as a CI-side scan that races two concurrent ADR-adding merges (check-then-act TOCTOU), so two ADRs still land with the same number — the named goal ('a new collision cannot merge') is not actually achieved
The LLM-Review vote is recorded but not bound to a tree SHA, so a re-push with a different tree carries the vote — 'provably attaches' is unmet

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a one-line positive rationale to each non-mechanical AC stating why the chosen mechanism fits (e.g. why CI enforcement over a runtime assertion/pre-commit hook, why binding the LLM-Review vote to `verified_at_sha`).
evidence: ABSENCE: header text is process provenance ('73 candidate findings... 27 survived a validity floor of 0.75'), not fitness rationale for any chosen fix
Every AC is phrased as a bare end-state ('...is deleted', '...is enforced by CI') with no 'because it fits X' clause
findings.finding: No acceptance criterion states a POSITIVE rationale for its chosen approach (why this fix/mechanism fits the codebase). The header explains the audit/verification PROCESS (blue-team floors, convergence), not why the specific remediations are the right approach. G6 checklist item 4 makes the absence of positive rationale a finding.
scenarios: An implementer or later reviewer cannot tell why e.g. CI enforcement was chosen over a runtime assertion or pre-commit hook for the snapshot-entry contract, and cannot sanity-check the fit
